title: the Pandavas' last journey, Yudhishthira's dog, heaven
hook: Yudhishthira reaches heaven and finds his old enemy enthroned there, and his brothers nowhere in sight
carry: the Pandavas' last journey, Yudhishthira's dog, heaven

segments.voice: Yesterday the Pandavas' last journey reached Indra's chariot, and Yudhishthira would not leave the dog, who turned out to be Dharma. Did you do a small kindness for someone who stuck with you? Day eight hundred seventy-eight.

The chariot sets him down in heaven, and the first face Yudhishthira sees is Duryodhana's. The cousin behind the rigged game of dice. The man who had Draupadi dragged into the hall. The one who would not make peace. He is sitting in splendor, honored among the gods. Yudhishthira's brothers are nowhere. Draupadi is nowhere. Karna is nowhere. And the man who refused heaven's chariot rather than abandon a dog now says, in effect, that he does not want this heaven. Take me to my brothers, he says. Wherever they are, that's where I want to be.
screen: `DURYODHANA, ENTHRONED.` → `NO BROTHERS. NO DRAUPADI.` → `"TAKE ME TO THEM."`

segments.voice: The sage Narada tries to calm him. This is heaven, he says; old quarrels end here. Duryodhana died fighting as a warrior, and this is where that leads. Yudhishthira won't be calmed. So the gods send a messenger to guide him to his family. The path turns dark. It smells of decay. There are thorns, burning things, bodies, a river that scalds. It is a hell. Yudhishthira has had enough, and turns to go back. And then voices call out of the dark. Stay, they beg him. While you stand here, a cool breeze blows and our pain eases. He asks who they are. Karna, they answer. Bhima. Arjuna. Nakula. Sahadeva. Dhrishtadyumna. Draupadi. The sons of Draupadi. Everyone he loved is here, in torment, while the man who caused the war sits on a throne. Yudhishthira is furious, at the gods and at dharma itself. And then he makes his choice. He tells the messenger to go back without him. If his presence comforts them, he will stay in hell. That is the moment it ends. Indra and the gods appear. The darkness lifts. It was an illusion, Indra explains; every king must glimpse hell, and Yudhishthira saw it because of his own deception in the war, about Drona's son. Dharma says his son has been tested once more and has held. Then Yudhishthira bathes in the heavenly Ganga, leaves his human body, and finds his brothers and Draupadi in their own true forms. The serial that began with a family quarrel ends with a man who would rather share his family's pain than enjoy a heaven without them.
screen: `NARADA: OLD QUARRELS END HERE` · `VOICES IN THE DARK: "STAY"` · `HE CHOOSES TO STAY IN HELL` · then, large: `THE ILLUSION LIFTS`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your hands rest. This is the end of a very long story, so give it a quiet minute. Breathe in, and bring to mind one person whose hard time you would rather share than be spared from. Breathe out, and let the wish to fix it loosen a little. Just stand near them in your mind, the way Yudhishthira stood in the dark. If you pray, you can hold them in your prayer. If not, just keep them company. The bell holds the time.
The Pandavas' last journey. It ends in heaven, after a king chooses to stand in hell beside the people he loves.

Your line: the Pandavas' last journey, Yudhishthira's dog, heaven. Today, keep someone company in a hard thing without trying to fix it. Tomorrow, a new story begins with a birth. Day eight hundred seventy-eight.

howItsDone: The Svargarohana Parva is the last book of the Mahabharata; Hindus hear its ending in recitations of the full epic, and some retellings of the epic linger on Yudhishthira's choice to stay with his family.

match.prompt: the last book — tap the pairs.

myth: Yudhishthira finds his brothers waiting on thrones
he finds Duryodhana enthroned and his brothers apparently in hell.
Yudhishthira decides to stay in hell with his family
he sends the messenger back without him, and then the illusion lifts.
Indra says the hell was real and permanent
he says it was an illusion, and that every king must glimpse hell.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. you can go back to heaven's comfort, or stay in a dark place where your presence eases your family's pain. what do you do?
options: stay in the dark with them.
demand the gods bring them up.
fork.reveal: he sends the messenger away and stays, and that choice is what ends the illusion.

original.note: svarga: heaven, the realm of Indra and the gods, where this book is set.

trapdoor: what you thought: the hero reaches heaven, and that's the happy ending.
what it means: he finds his enemy in heaven, his family in hell, and chooses hell with them.
what a scholar hears: it was an illusion; Indra says every king must glimpse hell, and Yudhishthira's came from his deception about Drona's son.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Svargarohana Parva: Duryodhana in heaven, Narada's counsel, the path to hell, the voices, Yudhishthira's choice, Indra's and Dharma's explanation, the bath in the heavenly Ganga

notes: All paraphrase of Ganguli; on-screen quotation marks mark glosses of speech, not quotations.
Confirm the list of voices in hell (Karna, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadi, and the sons of Draupadi).

Confirm Indra's explanation: that all kings must see hell, and that Yudhishthira was shown it because of his deception of Drona about Ashvatthama. The script says 'his own deception in the war, about Drona's son'.
Confirm Dharma's statement that this was a further test. Ganguli may number it as the third test; the number was left out.
Confirm the bath in the heavenly Ganga (Mandakini) and Yudhishthira's casting off his human body.
This is the last day of the 'Mahabharata as a serial' part; the closing sentence sums up the serial without claims about its length or date.
Editor pass: review question now matches yesterday's carry; hook no longer says Duryodhana himself cheated at dice (Shakuni threw the dice) or that his pride 'started the war'.

Audit (2026-10-01): Yudhishthira did not walk away from heaven's door on day 877; he refused to board without the dog, so 'walked away' became 'refused heaven's chariot'. Ganguli's list of voices in hell includes Dhrishtadyumna between Sahadeva and Draupadi; added.
